questions.prompt: What is the correct value of the Winlogon Userinit registry entry?
questions.explanation: The trailing comma is genuine. Userinit accepts a comma-separated list and Windows runs every entry, which is exactly what an attacker exploits by appending a second path.

questions.prompt: Why do attackers append to Userinit rather than replacing it?
options: Replacing it is blocked by Windows
Appending preserves normal logon behavior so nothing visibly breaks, while replacement would be conspicuous
Appended entries run with higher privileges
questions.explanation: The original userinit.exe stays at the front of the string, so the logon completes normally and the addition is easy to overlook.

questions.prompt: Why does Winlogon helper execution timing favour the attacker?
options: It runs after all security tooling has fully loaded
It fires early in the logon sequence, potentially before some security tooling has finished initializing
It only runs during safe mode
questions.explanation: Executing before the desktop appears and before agents fully initialize is the same reasoning behind the Early Bird APC injection variant -- a window where monitoring may not yet be fully active.

questions.prompt: Why is a HKCU Winlogon override notable even when the HKLM values are clean?
options: HKCU values are ignored by Windows
It provides persistence for that one user and is invisible to an HKLM-only check
It requires administrative rights to create
questions.explanation: Per-user Winlogon values take effect for that user without needing elevation, so checking only the machine-wide key misses them entirely.
